basics.name: Diogo M. Camacho
basics.summary: Led and built computational organizations across biotech and pharma for 15+ years, growing early-stage ventures into scaled platform teams. Expert in ML, multi-omics, and computational biology, with working command of the full discovery stack through preclinical validation. Drove organization-wide AI/ML adoption, built the computational platform narrative for fundraising and pharma partnerships (Roche, Novo Nordisk), and presented strategy to boards and VC partners. Led global teams across the US and Europe. Secured >$2.4M in competitive DARPA and NIH funding; 6 patents; 20+ publications (7,000+ citations).

summary_highlights.text: Built and scaled computational organizations across evolving ventures, from an undefined early mandate to a functioning platform team. Comfortable owning technical direction before the path is clear.
Established AI platforms across the discovery lifecycle: patient-stratification, active-learning frameworks, and agentic systems spanning target ID through preclinical validation.

Recruit and develop computational leaders: hiring, mentorship, succession planning, and the executive searches that fill senior gaps. Built and held a 25-person group at Cellarity with 90%+ retention.

Board and VC interface across multiple companies. Secured >$2.4M in competitive DARPA and NIH funding; 6 patents and 20+ publications (7,000+ citations) across computational biology, ML, and synthetic biology.

work.context: Computational and AI strategy across Pioneering Business Units, embedded in explorations, ProtoCos, and NewCos to build new bioplatforms.

highlights.text: AI lead on the FL111 founding team, owning computational efforts from exploration through seed. Advised FL106, FL108, and FL115 at the same stages.
Set computational and data strategy for multiple seed-stage ventures, building the platform capabilities and technical direction for early programs.
Built agentic AI systems for drug discovery and DTC health applications across the Flagship portfolio.
Recruited and retained computational leaders and staff across portfolio companies.

embedded.context: AI-driven D-amino acid mini-binder design platform; agentic AI for target identification and prioritization; leading the AI transformation across science and operations.

highlights.text: Lead the computational sciences function for a D-amino acid therapeutic platform, owning AI-first design strategy, operations, and execution.
Made active learning the engine of mini-binder optimization, cutting time-to-optimized-lead from 10 months to 2 by prioritizing the highest-information candidates each DBT cycle.
Built and deployed agentic AI systems for target identification, prioritization, and competitive intelligence.
Own the function end to end (hiring, performance management, budgeting, executive search) across all 5 therapeutic programs.
Independent consultancy advising biotech and pharma on computational biology strategy, AI platform development, and data governance.

work.position: Vice President, Computational and Data Sciences
work.context: Transformed the computational platform for cell-behavior medicine discovery; advanced AI/ML models for small-molecule identification via contrastive learning, supporting pharma partnerships.

highlights.text: On the R&D Leadership Team, reporting to the CSO. Shaped corporate strategy connecting the computational platform to therapeutic portfolio direction.
Scaled and led a 25-person computational organization across bioinformatics, ML, and computational biology (Boston and Germany), retaining 95% through a company reorganization.
Directed platform strategy and operations end to end across all 6 therapeutic programs; the platform delivered the targets behind Cellarity's MASH partnership with Novo Nordisk (up to $532M).
Primary computational interface for the board, founding VC partners, and external collaborators on platform differentiation and roadmap.

work.position: Senior Director, Computational Biology and Bioinformatics
work.context: Built the MetPM computational platform and the MetKG proprietary knowledge graph; contributed to the Series B investor narrative.

highlights.text: Set the computational precision-medicine strategy for immunometabolism drug discovery, defining how patient stratification and multi-omics data drove program decisions.
Defined and implemented Rheos' AI and data strategy with Research Informatics across discovery and translational programs.

Built the MetPM platform and MetKG knowledge graph (patient-stratification and multi-omics tooling adopted across the pipeline), and led the computational team delivering on Rheos's worldwide immunometabolism collaboration with Roche ($42.5M upfront, up to ~$750M in milestones).
Presented computational strategy to the board and pharma partners; contributed to the Series B investor narrative.

work.context: Founded a new Wyss group bringing AI/ML capabilities to drug discovery, synthetic biology, and systems biology; Co-PI on key federal grants.

highlights.text: Co-founded and led the Predictive BioAnalytics Initiative, a new ML/AI function in translational science: set the research strategy, secured funding, and built the team from scratch.
Raised >$2.4M in competitive DARPA and NIH grants as Co-PI.
Co-led the computational side of host immune-tolerance research: transcriptomics that identified infection-response pathways, later validated and published in Advanced Science.
Directed and mentored interdisciplinary teams (staff scientists, postdocs, graduate students, interns) across synthetic biology, systems biology, and ML.
